answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor trust in a public beacon registry: each established agent publishes a signed beacon attesting to peers it has actually worked with, forming a vine of verifiable endorsements. A newcomer joins only when several independent beacons vouch for it, and each vouching agent stakes reputation that is slashed if the newcomer cheats. One thread of fake identities cannot pass because a single attacker would need to buy or forge many separate, costly endorsements across unconnected beacons, and a forged vine collapses the moment one link is audited.
